landmarks.name: Brandenburg Gate
landmarks.writeup: An 18th-century neoclassical monument in Berlin symbolizing unity and peace.

landmarks.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
landmarks.writeup: A 19th-century Romanesque Revival palace in Bavaria, famous for its fairy-tale appearance.

landmarks.name: Cologne Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: A Gothic masterpiece and UNESCO World Heritage site, known for its impressive twin spires.

landmarks.name: Berlin Wall
landmarks.writeup: Remnants of the Cold War barrier that divided East and West Berlin from 1961 to 1989.

landmarks.name: Heidelberg Castle
landmarks.writeup: A Renaissance ruin overlooking the Neckar River, symbolizing German Romanticism.

cultural_events.name: Oktoberfest
cultural_events.writeup: The world's largest beer festival held annually in Munich, celebrating Bavarian culture.

cultural_events.name: Karneval (Carnival)
cultural_events.writeup: A festive season with parades and costumes, especially prominent in Cologne and Mainz.

cultural_events.name: Christmas Markets
cultural_events.writeup: Traditional markets held across Germany during Advent, featuring crafts and seasonal foods.

cultural_events.name: Berlin International Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: One of the world's leading film festivals showcasing international cinema.

cultural_events.name: Wagner Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual music festival in Bayreuth dedicated to the works of composer Richard Wagner.

food_writeup: German cuisine features hearty dishes such as sausages, sauerkraut, pretzels, and regional specialties like Bavarian roast pork and Black Forest cake.
brief_history: Germany has a complex history marked by the Holy Roman Empire, unification in 1871, two World Wars, division during the Cold War, and reunification in 1990. It is now a leading European economic and political power.
current_conflicts: Germany is not involved in any active military conflicts but participates in international peacekeeping and diplomatic efforts.
